newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Ferrum sees higher 1997 group net profit.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Ferrum sees higher 1997 group net profit.

text.p: Polish metal pipe maker Huta Ferrum plans expects its group net profit to rise to 6.5 million zlotys in 1997 from 4.48 million last year, the company's president said on Monday.
Jan Korzeniec told a news conference Ferrum upheld its earlier forecast of a 4.8 million zloty non-consolidated net profit.
He also said Ferrum would seek to diversify its production to gain access to new foreign markets,
"We aim to diversify our activities so as to enter markets still new for us", Jan Korzeniec told a news conference. @
He said the company planned to invest 26.2 million marks to launch a new line of steel pipes with cement inner coating designed for carrying drinking water.

Huta Ferrum, which starts trading on the Warsaw bourse's main market on June 27, will finance one-third of the project with proceeds from its 33-million zloty public offering and the rest from commercial credits, Korzeniec said.
It recently signed a long-term credit contract for 14.7 million marks with Bank Slaski SA in Katowice.
Korzeniec said the firm was also laying stress on ensuring its technologies are environmentally-friendly.
